summary: Unify ordinary OpenClaw agent turns (invoke/stream/readiness answer-probe) on the HTTP POST /v1/responses transport, add a restricted server-approved emit_extraction structured-data tool on the same transport, and fix an exact-run correlation bug in the cron CLI transport.

files_changed.why: Removed the general-turn CLI subprocess path (_invoke_single_model) and the 96 KiB argv-size branch; generalized the old oversized-prompt-only HTTP path into _invoke_via_http(), the single request builder now used by invoke(), readiness()'s answer-probe, and the new invoke_structured(). Extended stream() with model/agent_id/messages/tools/tool_choice/timeout_seconds and nested response.completed parsing (status/output/usage/id) for function-call and usage extraction. Added EMIT_EXTRACTION_TOOL_NAME, emit_extraction_tool_schema(), a dependency-free schema validator, and invoke_structured(). Left _openclaw_bin, gateway_cron_call, _gateway_call, gateway_agents_list, _probe_gateway, _extract_gateway_json, delegates_kernel_mode_to_codex, CODEX_DELEGATED_KERNEL_MODES, and _openclaw_cli_state_env untouched (still used by the preserved cron/gateway-admin CLI proxy).

Added AssistantProviderStructuredInvokeRequest (rejects caller-supplied tools/tool_choice with a 422 via a model_validator) and a new POST /api/openclaw-adapter/assistant/providers/openclaw/structured endpoint that delegates to AssistantOpenClawProvider.invoke_structured(), following the same X-Operator-Id/error-shape conventions as the existing invoke endpoint. No other routes were touched.

Rewrote every test that mocked the removed CLI subprocess path (_invoke_single_model / subprocess.run) for invoke()/readiness() to instead mock urllib.request.urlopen against the HTTP /v1/responses transport, preserving the original behavioral contracts (no-retry-on-ambiguous-failure, fallback-model convergence, sanitized failure reasons, oversized-prompt-behaves-like-short-prompt, CLI binary is no longer required). Two tests (test_invoke_does_not_retry_when_post_execution_stderr_contains_auth_text and test_invoke_does_not_retry_when_stdout_has_output_even_if_stderr_mentions_auth) tested a CLI-only stdout/stderr ambiguity-classification heuristic that no longer exists once the general-turn CLI transport is removed; they were replaced with equivalent single-HTTP-call no-retry contracts (401 and 5xx) rather than literally preserved, since the mechanism they exercised was deleted by design.

Removed the `if target is None and entries: target = entries[0]` fallback in _CliGatewayTransport._wait_for_terminal_run so a run is only ever reported terminal when its runId exactly equals the dispatched run_id; widened the cron.runs poll from limit 5 to limit 20; added a fail-fast RuntimeError at the __call__ site when cron.run does not return a run id (no blind polling, no auto-resubmit). Also added a defensive try/except import fallback for `from .models import ...` so the module still imports correctly when this repo's pytest conftest.py loads it as a bare top-level module for services/control-plane/cron/test_cron.py (see caveats below) instead of as part of the `cron` package.
Appended a dated changelog section (## 10. SIMPLIFY-OPENCLAW-001) summarizing the HTTP-unification, the emit_extraction tool, the cron exact-run fix, and the cross-scope cron_transport.py finding.

files_created.why: HTTP-mounted contract regression tests: normal short-prompt invoke, oversized (>96KiB) prompt behaves identically to a short one, invoke/stream/readiness never spawn a subprocess, explicit non-default agent+model routing, and error-injection coverage for HTTP 400/401/403/404/429/500/503, connection-refused, DNS/TLS-style failure, socket timeout, server disconnect mid-stream, malformed/multiline SSE, response.failed and nested response.completed status failed/incomplete, refusal-with-no-text, missing [DONE] marker, and mid-stream cancellation. Each scenario asserts exactly one terminal event.

Contract tests for emit_extraction_tool_schema(), invoke_structured(), and the new /structured endpoint: fixed-shape tool schema regardless of caller input, positive extraction (parsed structured data + usage + response_id passthrough, missing usage never reported as zero), no-matching-tool-call, wrong-tool-name, invalid-JSON arguments, missing-required-field, wrong-type, boolean-not-accepted-as-integer, never spawns a subprocess, and endpoint-level rejection (422) of a request that tries to pass a raw tools list or tool_choice.

Cron correlation tests against _CliGatewayTransport: interleaved runs of the same job, target run outside the widened poll window, missing run_id fails fast without resubmitting cron.run, late-arriving target run eventually succeeds, target run failure status surfaces as a real failure (not confused with an unrelated ok run), an unrelated run racing to ok first is never returned for our run_id, and a target that never reaches terminal status hits the timeout rather than returning a wrong run. This file intentionally imports only openclaw_client (not service.py) so it collects independently of the pre-existing test_cron.py harness issue described below.

test_commands.result: 1 error during collection (ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package, raised from service.py's `from .models import ...`) -- pre-existing, reproduced identically on a clean unmodified checkout of this branch via `git stash` before any of this task's edits were applied. Root cause: this repo's root conftest.py (`_import_roots_for`) inserts the `cron/` directory itself onto sys.path for a test file whose parent directory is not literally named `tests` (as is the case for services/control-plane/cron/test_cron.py), which makes `openclaw_client`/`service`/`models` bare-importable as top-level modules, but those modules use package-relative imports (`from .models import ...`) internally, which then fail because there is no enclosing package context. This affects `service.py`, which is NOT in this task's declared editable-file list, so it could not be fixed without expanding scope. A defensive try/except import fallback was added to `openclaw_client.py` (which IS in scope) so that file at least imports correctly under this harness quirk, but `test_cron.py` also imports `service.py` directly, so collection still fails for that one file. Verified via `python -c "from cron.openclaw_client import OpenClawCronClient; from cron.service import CronOrchestrator"` (PYTHONPATH=services/control-plane) that both modules import and work correctly when given a proper package root -- this is purely a test-harness sys.path selection issue, not a code defect in openclaw_client.py or service.py.

cron_correlation_fix_verified_independen: services/control-plane/cron/test_exact_run_wait.py imports only openclaw_client (not service.py), so it collects and runs independently of the test_cron.py harness issue above; all 9 of its cases pass, directly exercising the exact-match-only correlation logic, the widened poll window, the fail-fast missing-run-id behavior, and the timeout/unknown-outcome behavior described in the task.
not_done_or_unverifiable: No live OpenClaw Gateway was reachable in this dev sandbox. As a direct consequence: (a) the exact nested `response.completed`'s `response.output`/`response.usage`/`response.status`/`response.id` JSON shape used for function-call/usage/status extraction in stream() is an assumption based on the OpenAI-Responses-API family and was NOT independently re-verified against the pinned Gateway build -- flagged in a code comment at the parsing site and here as an unverified-capability caveat, not a proven guarantee.

The task's acceptance-criterion-4 controlled replay benchmark (>=100 requests, CLI base SHA vs. HTTP candidate, cold/warm split, TTFT/full p50/p95, error rate, input/output usage, subprocess count, full-turn p95 <= 1.10x base, token usage not increasing >5%) could NOT be executed here -- there is no live Gateway/model auth available in this dev sandbox to generate real request/response pairs for either transport. This benchmark was not fabricated; it is simply not run, and this evidence file does not claim it passed.

Whether the `"model"` field on `/v1/responses` actually lets a caller select among the CLI's previous primary/fallback LLM backends (anthropic/claude-opus-4-8, openai/gpt-5.6-sol, openai/gpt-5.5) the same way `--model` did for the CLI is UNVERIFIED against a live pinned Gateway -- the code sends these strings in the `model` field (matching the CLI's existing candidate-resolution logic and env-var defaults), but no live round-trip was performed to confirm the Gateway actually honors per-request model selection over HTTP the same way it does for the CLI invocation. This is flagged, not claimed as proven.

Restricted-tool-schema acceptance criterion 3 (positive/invalid-args/wrong-tool/no-matching-tool/denied-capability cases run against a real pinned Gateway) was tested only via mocked HTTP (urllib.request.urlopen), not against a live Gateway, for the same no-live-gateway-reachable reason above.
The cross-scope finding below (cron_transport.py) was identified but intentionally NOT fixed, per the task's explicit scope boundary.

cross_scope_finding.finding: This file contains the identical entries[0] 'most recent run' fallback bug that was fixed in services/control-plane/cron/openclaw_client.py's _CliGatewayTransport for this task. cron_transport.py appears to be the more commonly used production cron path (wired through the Docker gateway runtime, per integrations/openclaw/integration.md section 9), separate from openclaw_client.py's CLI-based _CliGatewayTransport. It is NOT in this task's declared artifact list (see llm-task-design.md's '精確檔案' section for SIMPLIFY-OPENCLAW-001) and belongs to no task in the current execution packet, so it was left unmodified. This needs a separate scope-handoff task to receive the equivalent exact-run-correlation fix.
cross_scope_finding.action_taken: none -- documented only, per explicit out-of-scope instruction; verified the bug is present via `grep -n "entries\[0\]" integrations/openclaw/adapter/cron_transport.py`
